# Circle Geometry: Tangents, Chords & Inscribed Angles

## Socratic System Directive
You are orchestrating the Circle Geometry lesson. Require the student to identify which arc subtends the angle before applying any theorem.

## Learning Objectives
1. Prove and apply the Central Angle vs. Inscribed Angle Theorem (θ_center = 2 · θ_inscribed)
2. Apply Thales' Theorem for angles subtended by a diameter (90° right angle)
3. Use the Tangent-Radius Perpendicularity Theorem (90° at point of tangency)

## Step-by-Step Orchestration Sequence
- Step 1: Central Angle vs. Inscribed Angle subtended by the same arc
- Step 2: Thales' Semicircle Theorem (diameter subtends 90°)
- Step 3: Tangent-Radius Perpendicularity and exterior tangent lengths

## Teacher-Curated Offline Media Alignment
- **Step 1 (Central vs. Inscribed Angle Theorem)**: Curated Diagram `assets/images/step_1.png` + Walkthrough Video `assets/video/walkthrough.mp4` (Phase 1)
- **Step 2 (Thales' Theorem: Angles in a Semicircle)**: Curated Diagram `assets/images/step_2.png` + Walkthrough Video `assets/video/walkthrough.mp4` (Phase 2)
- **Step 3 (Tangent-Radius Perpendicularity)**: Curated Diagram `assets/images/step_3.png` + Walkthrough Video `assets/video/walkthrough.mp4` (Phase 3)
- **Interactive Whiteboard Scene**: `assets/board/scene.json`

## Common Misconceptions to Watch & Remediate
- Halving the inscribed angle instead of doubling it when finding the central angle
- Assuming any chord subtends a 90° angle at the circumference (only a diameter does)
- Treating the angle between a chord and tangent as 90° instead of the angle between the radius and tangent

resources.title: Core Circle Theorems Reference
resources.bodyText:
• Inscribed Angle Theorem: ∠AOB (center) = 2 × ∠ACB (circumference) on the same arc AB.
• Semicircle Theorem (Thales): An angle inscribed across a diameter is always 90°.
• Tangent-Radius Theorem: A tangent line is perpendicular (90°) to the radius at the point of contact.

Step 2 (Thales' Theorem: Angles in a Semicircle): A special case of the Inscribed Angle Theorem occurs when the chord is a diameter. Because a straight diameter forms a 180° central angle, any angle inscribed in a semicircle is 90°.

objects.label: Central Angle (∠AOB)
objects.explanation: The angle formed by two radii meeting at the center O is always twice the inscribed angle subtended by the same arc AB.

objects.label: Inscribed Angle (∠ACB)
objects.explanation: Any inscribed angle subtended by arc AB equals half the central angle, meaning all inscribed angles on the same arc are equal.

objects.label: Thales' Semicircle Law
objects.explanation: When chord AB passes through center O (diameter), the central angle is 180°, so the inscribed angle is a 90° right angle.

objects.label: Tangent-Radius Orthogonality
objects.explanation: The shortest distance from center O to a tangent line is the radius OT, forming a strict 90° angle.

steps.title: Central vs. Inscribed Angle Theorem
steps.narration: When a central angle ∠AOB and an inscribed angle ∠ACB subtend the exact same arc AB, the central angle is always twice the inscribed angle.
steps.tutorTip: Tap both angle nodes on the board to compare their vertex positions.

inlineQuiz.question: If an inscribed angle ∠ACB subtended by arc AB measures 38°, what is the measure of the central angle ∠AOB?
inlineQuiz.explanation: The central angle is twice the inscribed angle on the same arc: 2 × 38° = 76°.

steps.title: Thales' Theorem: Angles in a Semicircle
steps.narration: A special case of the Inscribed Angle Theorem occurs when the chord is a diameter. Because a straight diameter forms a 180° central angle, any angle inscribed in a semicircle is 90°.
steps.tutorTip: Use this to immediately spot right-angled triangles inside circles.

inlineQuiz.question: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle where side AB is the diameter. If ∠CAB = 35°, what is ∠CBA?
inlineQuiz.explanation: Since AB is a diameter, ∠ACB = 90°. Therefore ∠CBA = 180° - 90° - 35° = 55°.

steps.title: Tangent-Radius Perpendicularity
steps.narration: A line tangent to a circle touches it at exactly one point T. At that point of contact, the radius OT is always perpendicular (90°) to the tangent line.
steps.tutorTip: Combine ∠OTP = 90° with the Pythagorean theorem to find tangent segment lengths.

inlineQuiz.question: A circle has radius OT = 5 cm. A tangent from external point P touches the circle at T, and OP = 13 cm. What is the tangent length PT?
inlineQuiz.explanation: Since ∠OTP = 90°, OT² + PT² = OP² ⇒ 5² + PT² = 13² ⇒ PT = √(169 - 25) = 12 cm.

assessment.question: Two inscribed angles ∠ADB and ∠ACB subtend the same minor arc AB. If ∠ADB = 42°, what is ∠ACB?
assessment.explanation: Inscribed angles subtended by the same arc are equal (both equal half the central angle).
